picks.title: AI models simulate a wider range of real-world scenarios
picks.excerpt: MIT's GeoPT is a pretraining method that gives simulation models a working feel for physics and geometry before task training. It generalizes to unseen scenarios like crash tests and aerodynamics while needing up to 60% less training data.
picks.rationale: Freshest, most concrete result in the pool: pretraining a simulator on geometry and physics first cuts training data by up to 60% and generalizes to crash and aero cases, which is exactly the bottleneck that keeps AI simulation out of everyday product design.

picks.title: AI model captures how humans read, paving the way for personalized text
picks.excerpt: Aalto University trained a reinforcement-learning model of human reading whose attention decisions matched real eye-tracking data, published in Nature Human Behaviour. The team says it explains rather than mimics reading, opening the door to per-reader text layout and AR displays.
picks.rationale: A model that explains rather than imitates eye movement turns typography and layout into something you can simulate per reader — the most directly design-actionable science item of the week, and Nature Human Behaviour gives it weight.

picks.title: AI agents for science: why reasoning beats more data
picks.excerpt: The argument: AI for science has to move past data-hungry models like AlphaFold toward reasoning agents that use tools, revise as evidence arrives, and mirror how research actually proceeds. Agents drastically reduce the need for scarce, specialized scientific datasets.
picks.rationale: Names the shift the last two weeks of lab-automation stories have been circling — from scaling datasets to agents that reason with tools — and lands the day after DeepMind wound down the AlphaFold team, giving the argument unusual timing.

picks.title: Q&A: AI chatbot use for mental health is surging among teens
picks.excerpt: Harvard researchers report AI chatbot use for mental health among 12-21 year olds jumped from about 1 in 8 to nearly 1 in 5 in a single year. Most users tell neither parents nor clinicians, even though general-purpose chatbots are unvalidated for this use.
picks.rationale: One in eight to nearly one in five teens in a single year, mostly hidden from parents and clinicians — a hard number showing general-purpose chatbots have already become de facto mental-health products without being designed or validated as such.

picks.title: AI model detects three types of cardiac dysfunction from a standard ECG
picks.source: EurekAlert (Wake Forest University School of Medicine)
picks.excerpt: Wake Forest researchers trained an AI model that reads standard ECGs to detect three types of cardiac dysfunction, including heart failure with preserved ejection fraction that routine care often misses. It held up on single-lead data of the kind wearables capture.
picks.rationale: The result that matters is the single-lead finding: it holds on the kind of trace a smartwatch already records, which moves an underdiagnosed heart-failure screen from the clinic onto the wrist.
